rationale: Intake: 'session quality is inconsistent' — the process is currently negotiated per session.
statement: The system must define the sequence of planning activities and their completion conditions, such that two planning sessions on comparable projects follow the same sequence.
title: The planning process is defined by the system, not by the session

rationale: Intake: the PM cannot currently tell how far a planning session has got.
statement: At any point the system must be able to report which stage the project is in and what that stage still requires.
title: Current project state is inspectable at any time

rationale: Intake problem 2: 'educated guessing' on vendor docs, OS procedures, versions and known issues.
statement: When a planning question depends on external fact, the system must be able to consult a current external source rather than reason from what it already holds.
title: Implementation questions can be answered from current external sources

rationale: Without this the distinction between a documented claim and a guess is lost the moment it is written down.
statement: Any claim the plan rests on that came from an external source must record a reference to that source.
title: A claim taken from a source records that source

rationale: Intake problem 3: no sandbox, so testable assumptions are inferred instead.
statement: The system must be able to execute a procedure in a real environment and capture the commands run, the output produced, and whether it succeeded.
title: Claims can be tested by execution in a real environment

rationale: A procedure that worked somewhere unlike the target has not been validated for the target.
statement: Any claim validated by execution must record the environment it ran in, in enough detail to judge whether that environment resembles the target.
title: A tested claim records the environment it was tested in

rationale: Intake's central constraint: a guess, a documented claim and a demonstrated one must remain distinguishable to the end.
statement: Every claim the plan depends on must carry a recorded basis — unverified, source-supported, or demonstrated by execution — as structured data rather than prose.
title: Every load-bearing claim carries how it is known

rationale: If telling them apart requires careful reading, it will not survive contact with a long document.
statement: A reader or a consuming agent must be able to tell the basis of any claim by inspecting structure, without interpreting narrative text.
title: A reader can distinguish claim strength without reading prose

rationale: Intake: 'the runbook should represent the output of discovery, not the beginning of discovery.'
statement: No instruction in the final output may rest on a claim whose basis is below the level required for that instruction.
title: Instructions rest on resolved claims

rationale: Intake objective, stated in the PM's own terms.
statement: A recipient of the output must be able to begin their part of the work without asking the planner for information the plan should have contained.
title: The handoff is actionable without returning to the planner

rationale: Intake stakeholders: the material explicitly declines to assume which the implementer is. This is testable by comparing both consumers against the same required-information inventory.
statement: For every required item in the handoff, both a human reader and an automated consumer must be able to recover the same information without depending on the other representation.
title: The output serves a human or an agent implementer

rationale: Intake constraint: validation cannot assume a free, local, consequence-free environment.
statement: The system must not perform a validation that incurs cost or uses credentials unless the operator has explicitly authorised that class of validation.
title: Validation that costs money or needs credentials requires explicit authorisation

rationale: Intake: 'continuously capture decisions and evolving requirements.' A decision without alternatives cannot be reopened intelligently.
statement: Every decision that shapes the plan must be recorded together with the options considered and why the chosen one won.
title: Decisions are recorded with their alternatives

rationale: Intake open questions 1-4 are themselves examples: they need to survive being read once.
statement: An unresolved question must exist as a tracked item with a state, not as a sentence inside a document.
title: Open questions are tracked objects, not prose

rationale: Retired during PM review: local single-operator operation is a later architecture decision, not a constraint stated by the frozen intake. Keeping it here would back-project the chosen solution into the solution-free ask.
statement: The system must be usable by one operator on one machine with no hosted service required.
title: The system runs locally for a single operator

rationale: REQ-0002 requires current project state to be inspectable at any time, and stage position is the coarsest form of that state. Deriving it rather than storing it follows #16: stage status is derived from artifacts, never persisted alongside them.
statement: The application shows which stage the project is in, derived from the stage definitions and the recorded attestations rather than from a stored status value.
title: The application displays the project's current stage

rationale: Stage documents are the narrative half of the plan and are agent-authored. Rendering them is the point of choosing MDX; bounding what they may execute is what keeps content from becoming application code.
statement: The application renders the MDX stage document for a selected stage, and a document referencing a component outside the permitted set does not execute arbitrary code.
title: The application renders a stage document authored in MDX

rationale: The agent and the operator write the same files (#15), so a view that only refreshes on reload shows state that has already moved. The second clause is the harder half: a silently dead stream renders stale content that looks live.
statement: When a file under the content root is changed by something other than the application, the application's view updates without the operator reloading the page, and a dropped update stream is visibly distinguishable from an idle one.
title: The application reflects external content changes without a manual reload

rationale: #88 forbids authoring content by any route but a typed operation, and #78 plus #72 make the write safe against the agent writing concurrently. A second write path in the app would be a second protocol against the same files.
statement: A review-status change made in the application is written by the existing typed operation — lock, fresh read inside the lock, atomic write — and the application contains no other write path into content.
title: The application performs review-status updates through the existing typed write path

rationale: The product is a local-first tool a consumer clones (#1, #20, #32). An application whose supported mode is undeclared cannot be validated against the configuration it actually ships in — which is why AST-0010 is deferred rather than answered.
statement: An operator can install and start the application on a clean machine from documented commands, and the supported deployment mode is stated rather than implied.
title: The application is installable and runnable locally from a documented command

notes: ⚠️ THIS IS AN ARCHITECTURAL REQUIREMENT, NOT A TESTING PREFERENCE, and the distinction is what AST-0022 establishes. 'Verify it behaves correctly' is unavailable here as a matter of measured fact rather than of rigour — the observable behaviour of a compliant and a non-compliant read is IDENTICAL on a route that has at least one compliant read. The property has to be enforced where it is visible, which is in the source. ⚠️ TWO OBLIGATIONS, and the second is the one that gets forgotten: confine the read, AND check the boundary. DEC-0019 requires both `connection()` before the read and a `<Suspense>` boundary around it, and an abstraction can supply the first while a caller omits the second. A check that only looks for stray `readFileSync` calls would pass an application whose every read is correctly routed and unboundaried — which builds fine without Cache Components and FAILS THE BUILD with it, so the omission surfaces as a configuration change breaking the build rather than as the contract violation it is. ⚠️ THE MECHANISM IS DELIBERATELY UNSPECIFIED. A lint rule, a module-boundary constraint, a generated single accessor, or a build step that greps for content-root paths would each satisfy this; choosing among them is stage 5 design work that belongs with the components, and naming one here would decide it before the components exist. What is fixed is the PROPERTY: checkable without executing the application. ⚠️ IT INTERACTS WITH QST-0018 AND DOES NOT PRE-EMPT IT. If a stage document may reference components, then the permitted-component set is also a surface through which a direct read could enter, and static confinement has to cover it. That is a constraint QST-0018's answer must satisfy, not a decision about what that answer is. ⚠️ IT DOES NOT SETTLE CACHE COMPONENTS. DEC-0019 was chosen precisely so the contract holds with that flag either way, and a static check on source has nothing to say about it. Any enforcement design that only works under one setting would spend the property DEC-0019 bought. ⚠️ SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-08-27 BY DEC-0021: the same static check must also enforce that no application module outside `app/server/` imports from `lib/`, and must detect bypass paths. It is one more forbidden edge in the same import graph, not a second mechanism — and it is the same failure shape as AST-0022, because the adapter boundary is a convention that nothing observable distinguishes from a violation: an app module importing `lib/` directly behaves identically until someone renders it from a client component.
rationale: AST-0022 measured that a read violating the contract is served FRESH whenever a compliant read shares its route — the compliant read makes the route dynamic and the violation rides along. So a behavioural check cannot see the violation: every freshness test passes on a codebase that breaks the contract, right up until the compliant sibling is moved, cached or deleted, at which point every read on that route silently reverts to build-time content. A test that passes on broken code is worse than no test, because it is also a claim that the code was checked.
statement: Every read of planning content in the application goes through a single reading abstraction that applies the DEC-0019 contract. A direct filesystem read of the content root anywhere else in the application fails a check that does not depend on running the application or observing what it serves, and the same check verifies that each read site is enclosed by a `<Suspense>` boundary. Acceptance for REQ-0016, REQ-0017 and REQ-0018 may not rest on freshness behaviour alone.
title: Planning-content reads are confined to the approved abstraction, and the confinement is checked statically

notes: ⚠️ THE REFUSAL HALF IS NOT DECORATION. Setup touches an operator's credentials, trust store, ports and money; the number of ways it can legitimately stop is larger than the number of ways it can succeed. A command that succeeds or hangs is worse than one that refuses precisely, which is why the phase and the resume command are in the statement rather than in the error-handling section of a design document.
rationale: The product is a planning conversation that writes structured content and shows it in a browser. Until 2026-09-02 the documented consumer path ended at `npm --prefix .planning start`, which starts the browser and nothing else: Pi started nowhere, so the half of the product that does the planning was unreachable by any documented route. A requirement that says `installable and runnable` (REQ-0020) was satisfied by that state, which is how the gap stayed invisible.
statement: From a machine that has Git and the supported Node version and nothing else of Kiln's, one documented command must initialise the planning workspace, install the pinned agent runtime, obtain every decision it needs from the operator, and end with the planning agent conversing about this project — or refuse, naming the phase that stopped and an exact command that resumes it. Starting the browser application alone does not satisfy this requirement.
title: One documented command carries a clean project to a running planning conversation

notes: ⚠️ 'RECORDED WHERE ANOTHER OPERATOR DOES NOT INHERIT IT' IS THE HALF THAT IS EASY TO LOSE. The project selection is committed configuration and should be; the approval to use THIS host's credentials is not. If the two are stored together, cloning the repository hands a second operator the first operator's consent, and nobody ever sees the prompt.
rationale: Technical access is not consent. Kiln runs on the operator's own machine and can read their Pi configuration trivially, which is exactly why the boundary has to be a decision rather than a capability check. The three permissions are genuinely different questions — a local inspection that contacts nothing, an ongoing authorisation to spend on a named model, and an external call to a third-party service — and collapsing them into one prompt would mean the operator granting the expensive one by answering the cheap one.
statement: The system must not read the operator's provider authentication store, custom-model registry, or the presence of credential environment variables before the operator has permitted that inspection. Having detected a usable configuration must never by itself authorise adopting or using it. Permission to inspect, confirmation of an exact provider and model, and permission to validate and use an optional external service are three decisions, each granted separately and each recorded where a different operator on a different machine does not inherit it.
title: Existing configuration is inspected, and then used, only under separately granted permission

notes: ⚠️ PROCESS ARGUMENTS ARE IN THE LIST DELIBERATELY. Command lines are visible in process listings to other users on the same machine, so passing a key through Pi's `--api-key` option is a disclosure even though nothing is written to disk. ⚠️ SO ARE DERIVED VALUES: a hash or prefix of a key recorded as a cache identity is credential-derived, and a compatibility record keyed on one is a credential artifact wearing a different name.
rationale: The specialist child environment is the concrete hazard. The existing contract passes base OS variables plus TAVILY_API_KEY for the research role, which is correct for the tool plane and insufficient for the model plane: a provider authenticated only through OPENAI_API_KEY leaves every child unable to infer. The tempting fix — inherit more of the environment — is the one that must be foreclosed by a requirement, because it works immediately and leaks everything.
statement: No committed project file, emitted log line, error message, generated artifact, test fixture, or constructed process argument may contain a credential value or a value derived from one. A credential reaches a subprocess only through an audited contract that names, for one selected provider, the exact environment-variable names required; a provider with no such recorded mapping is refused rather than granted a wider inheritance of the operator's environment.
title: Credential material never enters project files, logs, process arguments, or planning content

notes: ⚠️ 'EXPLICITLY SELECTED' BINDS EVEN WHEN DISCOVERY RETURNS EXACTLY ONE MODEL. A single available model is a discovery result, not a decision, and adopting it silently is the same class of act as adopting the global default. ⚠️ THE PROOF COSTS MONEY, which is why it is a separate authorisation and not a step: see the consent requirement.
rationale: Two silent failures are being closed at once. A registry entry proves configuration and not that the endpoint answers or that the model will emit a correctly shaped tool call, so a zero-cost preflight cannot be the last word. And a fallback to a global default would mean the project's recorded content was produced by a model the project never named, which destroys the only reproducibility claim the configuration makes.
statement: The provider and exact model used for planning work must be chosen by the operator from what discovery reports, recorded as reproducible non-secret project configuration naming exact identifiers rather than a mutable alias, and proven able to perform the tool calls the system depends on before the system describes the agent as ready. When the recorded selection cannot be resolved or authenticated, the system must refuse to begin or resume planning work rather than substituting another model, another provider, or its own memory.
title: Agent work runs on an explicitly selected and proven model, or it does not run

notes: ⚠️ THIS IS THE OPEN HALF OF DECISION #67. Half of that decision — recording a trust grant so children come up trusted — has been executed and measured. The detection half has never been built, and it is the half that holds when the grant is missing, revoked, or made on a different machine.
rationale: Measured on 2026-08-15 and not since mitigated: a non-interactive Pi child launched against an untrusted project loads no package, therefore none of Kiln's typed tools, and DOES NOT ERROR. The session completes, turn_start and turn_end and agent_end all fire, and the model answers in freehand prose. Every role boundary in this system is enforced by typed tools, so a child without them is not a degraded specialist — it is an unconstrained model whose output looks exactly like a specialist's.
statement: Before any part of a specialist's substantive answer is read or acted on, the system must observe that the child ran with the capability signature and tool set its role contract requires. A child that exited cleanly, emitted a well-formed transcript, and did not have those tools must fail the delegation loudly; its prose must not be accepted as the answer to the delegated task.
title: A delegated result is used only when the child that produced it is proven to have had its tools

notes: ⚠️ THE ORDERING IS THE OPERATIONAL HALF. A design that puts transcripts under an ignored path is correct and still leaks if the first transcript is written before the ignore rule exists, or if the operator deleted the rule and setup carried on. The safe sequence and the refusal that follows a missing rule are both part of the requirement.
rationale: The tool clone at `.planning/` is updated with `git pull`, so anything runtime written inside it is state the update channel is entitled to destroy. The outer project is version-controlled by the operator, so anything runtime written there is state Git is entitled to publish. Both halves of that sentence have to hold at once, which is why the requirement names an ordering — coverage first, then data — rather than only a location.
statement: Session transcripts, launch state, consent records, compatibility results and setup journals must be written where updating the tool clone cannot destroy them and where ordinary version control does not track them, while reproducible non-secret project configuration remains committed and reviewable. The system must not write runtime state into a location before the ignore coverage protecting that location is in place.
title: Runtime state survives a tool update and never enters version control

notes: ⚠️ THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS TESTABLE, and it should be written before the check: stand up an unrelated healthy HTTP server on the port and require launch to refuse. A readiness check without that control has never been shown to check anything.
rationale: The current launcher polls `GET /` on the configured port and treats any HTTP response as ready. An unrelated service already listening on port 3000 therefore satisfies it, and the operator is told the browser workspace is up while looking at somebody else's application. The same shape recurs across the layer: an extension that loaded, a model that replied, a session that resumed — each is only evidence if something distinguishes it from a lookalike.
statement: Before reporting a component ready, the system must confirm the identity of whatever responded: that the HTTP service answering the port is the process this invocation started and is serving this project, that the loaded package is the one it installed, and that the model answering is the one recorded. A response that merely arrives, from an unidentified source, is not readiness and must not be reported as such.
title: A readiness claim names what answered
